name: Anti-racism
summary: Anti-racism opposes racism and racial discrimination in law, institutions and ideas. Its programmatic texts (the UN's ICERD and Durban Declaration) reject doctrines of racial superiority as false, require states to prohibit discrimination including by private persons, allow time-limited special measures, and condemn colonialism and slavery; Kendi's structural account judges policies by whether they produce racial equity. It has no economic, constitutional or foreign-policy programme of its own beyond these.
scope: Mainstream anti-racism as stated in three bodies of text: the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (1965), the Durban Declaration and Programme of Action (2001) adopted at the UN World Conference against Racism and Ibram X. Kendi's structural account (the How to Be an Antiracist excerpt and his 2019 NPR interviews, with Madva's scholarly summary of it). Madva (a philosophy paper on antiracists) is the scholarly source that names the ideology and Kendi; ICERD and the Durban texts use 'anti-racism' and 'racism' for the same cause. Excluded: Black Power and Black nationalism, socialist or feminist offshoots (the Combahee River Collective), and ethnic-nationalist movements. Their texts were not used, and the earlier audit's answers that rested on Wikipedia summaries or on those strands were nulled in this pass. Anti-racism has no stated programme on most economic, constitutional and foreign-policy questions, so those statements are null.

apologise-for-past-wrongs.rationale: The Durban Declaration (para. 101) notes states that have presented apologies, appreciates them, and calls on those that have not yet contributed to restoring victims' dignity to find appropriate ways to do so.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The Durban Declaration (paras. 5 and 49-50) values multiculturalism and respect for migrants' differences of language, customs and culture, and treats integration as a matter of harmony, not replacing one culture with another.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Durban Declaration (para. 14) says colonialism led to racism and must be condemned, and ICERD's preamble records the UN's condemnation of colonialism and its discrimination.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Durban Declaration (paras. 14 and 99) condemns colonialism and its lasting economic and social inequalities; ICERD's preamble condemns colonialism in the same terms.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: ICERD Art. 1(4) and 2(2) allow and require special measures to secure equal enjoyment of rights, the Durban Declaration (para. 108) recognises the necessity of special measures for victims of racism, and Kendi calls antiracist discrimination the only remedy to past discrimination.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Madva reports Kendi's view that 'to be antiracist is to see all cultures in all their differences as on the same level, as equals'; the Durban Declaration (para. 6) affirms that all peoples form one human family rich in diversity.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: ICERD Art. 5(d)(iv) guarantees 'the right to marriage and choice of spouse' without racial distinction, and Art. 2(1)(e) tells states to discourage anything that strengthens racial division.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Kendi defines a racist policy as 'any measure that produces or sustains racial inequity between racial groups' and says he defines policy 'based on its effect' without regard to intent; ICERD Art. 1 likewise defines discrimination by 'purpose or effect'.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The Durban Declaration's preamble calls cultural diversity 'a cherished asset' that 'enriches our societies', and para. 6 says respect for diversity 'can produce more inclusive societies'.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Kendi writes that 'the only remedy to racist discrimination is antiracist discrimination' and the Durban Declaration (para. 108) holds special measures necessary; ICERD limits them in time (they end once their objectives are achieved) but does not call for abolishing them.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: ICERD's preamble holds that 'all human beings are equal before the law and are entitled to equal protection of the law', and Art. 5 guarantees equality before the law without distinction of race.

ethnicity-statistics.rationale: The Durban Programme of Action (para. 98) recommends that states report statistical information on groups and communities within their jurisdiction, collected under data-protection and privacy guarantees.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: ICERD Art. 2(1)(d) requires each state to prohibit and bring to an end racial discrimination 'by any persons, group or organization', by legislation where needed.

government-encourage-intercultural-conta.rationale: The Durban Declaration (paras. 49 and 82) calls for conditions of harmony and respect between migrants and the rest of society and for dialogue among civilizations.

hereditarian-race.rationale: ICERD and the Durban Declaration (para. 7) call any doctrine of racial superiority 'scientifically false' and reject theories of separate human races, and Kendi defines antiracist ideas as ideas of the equality of racial groups; none addresses measured ability gaps directly.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The Durban Declaration (para. 58) recalls 'that the Holocaust must never be forgotten', which treats the Holocaust as a recorded historical crime and is incompatible with denying it happened.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The Durban Programme of Action urges ending impunity and prosecuting those responsible for crimes against humanity and war crimes, and supports the international criminal tribunals and ratification of the Rome Statute.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The Durban Declaration (paras. 2 and 69) says victims can suffer multiple or aggravated discrimination and calls for integrating a gender perspective into measures against racism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The Durban Declaration (paras. 61 and 150) expresses concern at the rise of Islamophobia and 'discriminatory ideas' against Muslim communities and urges states to prevent movements based on them.

night-watchman-state.rationale: ICERD Art. 2 and the Durban Programme of Action assign states duties well beyond protection from physical violence: prohibiting private discrimination, education, health and development programmes.

population-transfer.rationale: ICERD Art. 5(d)(i)-(ii) guarantees freedom of movement and residence and the right to remain in one's country without distinction of race or ethnic origin, so expelling a group on those grounds is racial discrimination.

property-franchise.rationale: ICERD Art. 5(c) guarantees the right to vote 'on the basis of universal and equal suffrage', which a franchise limited to property owners would not meet.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: The Durban Declaration (para. 47) affirms each State's right to set migration policy but says it must be 'designed to ensure that [it is] free of racism, racial discrimination, xenophobia and related intolerance'.

race-social-construct.rationale: The Durban Declaration (para. 7) rejects 'theories which attempt to determine the existence of separate human races', and its preamble speaks of 'so-called distinct human races', treating racial categories as without scientific basis.

racial-franchise.rationale: ICERD Art. 5(c) guarantees political rights, 'to vote and to stand for election on the basis of universal and equal suffrage', without distinction as to race, colour or national or ethnic origin.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: ICERD Art. 3: 'States Parties particularly condemn racial segregation and apartheid and undertake to prevent, prohibit and eradicate all practices of this nature'.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The Durban Declaration (paras. 14, 18, 19) says racism and its legacies are closely tied to lasting inequality and underdevelopment, and Kendi holds that racist policies still produce racial inequity today.

remove-indigenous-peoples.rationale: The Durban Declaration (para. 43) recognises indigenous peoples' special relationship with their lands and encourages states to let them retain ownership of them.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: ICERD Art. 5(d) guarantees freedom of residence and the right to remain in one's country without racial distinction, and the Durban Declaration (para. 15) treats genocide as a crime against humanity and a major source of racism.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: ICERD Art. 4(a) makes 'all dissemination of ideas based on racial superiority or hatred' an offence punishable by law, though 'with due regard' to the Universal Declaration; the Durban Declaration (para. 87) repeats the duty. This covers racist speech, not every kind of hate speech.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The Durban Programme of Action (para. 158) calls for a new development partnership with the societies affected by historical injustices, including debt relief, poverty eradication and meeting official development assistance targets.

state-harmful.rationale: ICERD and the Durban Programme of Action rest on states legislating against and remedying discrimination (ICERD Art. 2), which contradicts abolishing the state.

missingStatements.text: Governments should review and repeal laws and policies that perpetuate racial discrimination in effect, even where no discriminatory intent exists.
missingStatements.rationale: ICERD defines discrimination by its purpose or effect and Art. 2(1)(c) requires states to amend or nullify laws that create or perpetuate it.

missingStatements.text: A policy should be judged racist if it produces racial inequity, whatever its intent.
missingStatements.rationale: Kendi defines racist policy as any policy that creates inequitable outcomes between racial groups, and the structural view treats intent as secondary.

notes: Themes searched in ICERD, the Durban Declaration and Kendi's texts: race and racism, special measures, colonialism and slavery, reparations and apologies, migration, indigenous peoples, hate speech and the internet, education, policing and justice, development and debt, democracy and political participation, language, gender, religion, Israel/Palestine. The Durban texts speak of reparation for victims of discrimination but only 'note' that some states paid reparation for slavery and colonialism, so the reparations statements are null. Statements on markets, ownership, taxes, guns, the family, religion in public life, war and most constitutional design have no position in these texts and are null; the earlier pass's 0 answers there recorded adherents differing, which is silence. King's Letter from Birmingham Jail was read, but no defining source ties it to anti-racism (the source check fails), so the answers resting on it were nulled; the Combahee statement and Carmichael's Black Power address were set aside as other movements' sources. Kendi's 2019 Politico proposal for an anti-racist constitutional amendment and a Department of Anti-racism was read; it settles no statement (a proposal limited to racial inequity, not a general position on experts or courts). Kendi's book itself was not available as full text; his positions come from the Penguin excerpt, two NPR interviews and Madva's scholarly report. This pass nulled answers resting on Wikipedia summaries (reviewHistory keeps the earlier versions) and is expected to leave the ideology below the uncertainty rule: that is the honest result of the record.

keyFigures.role: Historian and author of How to Be an Antiracist, whose structural account of racist policy is the best-known contemporary statement of anti-racism
keyFigures.quote: Kendi argues, for example, that antiracism requires endorsing radical cultural relativism.
